provenance.name: ccesMRPprep cd_info_2018 documentation
provenance.role: documents 435 contemporaneous 2018 districts and two-party McCain/Romney/Trump shares; Park-Egan fills Daily Kos 2008 gaps

provenance.name: FEC official election reports
provenance.role: official cross-check and frozen national D-R centring constants

transformations.district_presidential: ccesMRPprep Republican two-party shares converted to D-R margin as 100 - 2*R share; this matches the two-party district margin convention in the live upstream historical.csv.
transformations.state_presidential: MEDSL D and R candidate votes converted to D-R two-party state margin for Senate structural priors.
transformations.national_centring: Frozen FEC all-vote D-R national margins, matching the production model constants even though district/state structural margins are two-party margins.
transformations.poll_quality: FiveThirtyEight letter grades converted to a predeclared monotone 0.75-3.0 scale; missing grade=1.3. No election outcomes are used.
transformations.poll_availability: created_at is used only when it falls 0-14 days after poll end; otherwise publication_date is blank and Model Lab falls back to end_date.
transformations.multi_candidate_polls: Questions with multiple candidates on the same D/R side are excluded from binary race-poll blending.
transformations.aligned_independents: Angus King (ME-S1) and Bernie Sanders (VT-S1) are treated as Democratic-aligned for chamber-control outcome while raw incumbent party remains IND.
transformations.missing_result_party: When MEDSL party is neither DEM nor REP, the winner must match an unambiguous pre-election historical roster candidate; otherwise admission fails.

notes: FiveThirtyEight forecast probabilities and vote-share forecasts are never imported as MIDTERM SIGNALS predictive inputs.
Roster known_date comes from first appearance or subsequent candidate-set change in the archived daily FiveThirtyEight deluxe forecast.
MEDSL constituency returns supply machine-readable scoring outcomes and are checked against an independently preserved 2018 winner map.
The structural source is a pinned MIT-licensed academic data object whose documentation explicitly records contemporaneous 2018 geography and the source used to fill missing 2008 Daily Kos values.
